text:
jamal: Heads up — long-run load test on qwen-v2-dedicated produced steady mem growth even after prefixes cleared. kv pages keep increasing, plus ghost/unused slots piling up. Repro attached below.

priya: Can you paste the pprof/top snippet? any kernel-switch or fallback events in the logs?

jamal: pprof top (trimmed):
```
# total 16GB
1348.2MB  12.5%  kv_page_alloc
1024.6MB   9.5%  kv_page_retain
512.0MB    4.0%  attention_generic_kernel
256.1MB    2.0%  rope_scale_transform
```
Stack shows a lot of kv_page_alloc churn after ~6k tokens.

maria: hmm that smells like the coalescer not merging free ranges after kernel fallback. saw something similar with Llama-MQA when rope scale crossed 8192 — slab sizes mismatch.

kevin: I pulled the runtime logs for the same run — kernel-selection lines: 
```
[04:02:12] kernel_select: model=qwen-v2 seq=4096 -> using cuda_opt_attn
[04:02:13] kernel_select: seq=8192 -> fallback to generic_attention (kernel=generic_v2)
[04:03:05] kv: allocate slab id=0x7f8a size=2MB
[04:03:05] kv: allocate slab id=0x7f9c size=4MB
```
The fallback at 8192 changes slab allocator alignment, so previously adjacent free chunks no longer coalesce.

priya: Does the allocator track slab class per-kernel? Could be we end up with mixed-page-size freelists per kernel which blocks reuse.

jamal: Repro command I used: `./perf/run-loadgen --model qwen-v2 --seq_len=12000 --batch=1 --duration=30m --profile=kvcache`

maria: Also check kv journal for page residency timestamps — we saw long-lived shadow pages in MQA mode on Llama due to rope scaling remap. Quick grep: `grep -E "shadow|ghost|orphan" /var/log/runtime/kvcache/journal.log`

kevin: I ran that grep on the job container, snippet: 
```
[04:10:22] kvcache: mark_orphan page=0x3f2a age=932s reason=kernel-fallback
[04:12:01] kvcache: ghost_slot page=0x4b1c prev_owner=generic_v1
```
So pages are being orphaned by kernel variant transitions.

priya: Potential mitigation: when kernel switch happens, run a quick passive compaction pass to remap/merge adjacent free ranges across slab classes. Low-cost heuristic: only do it when seq_len > 4096 and free_ratio < 0.2.

jamal: Agreed. I'll try a prototype that triggers compaction on kernel-change events and measure overhead. If compaction too expensive, maybe we only compact pages older than X seconds.

maria: Also check batching heuristics — small batches keep KV pages hot; bigger batches cause KV reuse patterns to change and sometimes reveal fragmentation. Try ramping batch to 8 then 16 to compare.

kevin: One more data point: GQA vs MQA. On Llama-GQA we saw less fragmentation because interleaved multi-query leaves different page residency life; MQA had more contiguous allocation which paradoxically made coalescing harder when fallback occurred. Not sure on Qwen behaviour yet.

priya: Sounds like a multidimensional space: kernel-selection boundaries, rope scaling thresholds, and query-arch (GQA/MQA) interact. We should capture a small matrix test: 
- models: {llama-mqa, llama-gqa, qwen-v2} 
- seq: {4k, 8k, 12k} 
- batch: {1,8,16} 
Record: kv_free_ratio, ghost_slots, alloc_ops/sec, p99_rss.

jamal: I'll run the matrix overnight on staging and attach results. For immediate triage I'll push a lightweight compaction patch to the runtime branch (kvcache/compact-on-kernel-switch).

kevin: If you push, add a feature flag and perf metric so we can toggle and measure impact on latency tail. Don't forget to account for quantized models where slab sizes differ because of kernel quant path.

ops-bot: deploy: staging rollout started for commit ab12c3 (kvcache: compact-on-kernel-switch) — 2026-03-17T04:22:10Z

jamal: Thanks — patch pushed and rollout started. Will post matrix results + kv journal dumps when available. tagging @priya @maria for follow-ups. :eyes:
